abstract.text: Re-skin the engine’s stock lines, and roll dice that replay.

inlineContent.text: Every line the engine can say on its own initiative lives on one value,

inlineContent.text: All three draw from one stream whose position lives in the world state — with one exception worth knowing:
and
are not questions, so neither draws, and a daemon gated on either leaves the stream where it found it.
makes the opposite call and draws even for a single option, because its option count is a list an author edits and the stream must not notice the edit. That buys two guarantees:
Replays
: a world built with
plays out identically for the same seed and commands, on every platform — the backbone of transcript tests and reproducible bug reports. The plain
seeds fresh each run.
Saves
: the stream’s position is part of the saved state, so a restored game continues with exactly the randomness it would have had.
Pin the seed in a test the same way the engine’s own suite does:

code: let world = try GameWorld(game: MyGame(), seed: 42)

abstract.text: A phrase with its first letter capitalized, for a line that opens on
one. “the troll” becomes “The troll”; “Mrs. Vane” is already right.
Joins already-rendered phrases into an English list (“a Y”, “a Y and a
Z”, “a Y, a Z, and a W”). The articles are the caller’s, since only the
caller knows which of them are proper names.

A dark room, in answer to anything that would have needed the player to
see it: LOOK and the room describer, or a TAKE ALL whose group came back
empty because the dark had emptied it. The line most likely to want
: it prints on every dark turn, in every dark room, and
a game whose darkness has anything in it — a companion, a sound, a smell
— has to check that the thing is still there before saying so. Every
emitter says it through

still prints them once.
